ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: At the top of the figure is a carbonyl structure, the central carbon is connected to oxygen by a double bond, and the other two sides of the carbon are connected to R1 and R2 respectively; below is an amine structure, and the nitrogen is connected to H, R3, and R4. There are also curved arrows in the figure, but the question requires ignoring the arrows. Then reasoning: After ignoring the arrows, the structure can be viewed as two unconnected fragments: an R1-C(=O)-R2 carbonyl compound and an R3-N(H)-R4 amine. According to the method, replace each R group with the wildcard '*', write the carbonyl fragment as '*C(*)=O', write the amine fragment as '*N*', and connect the two unconnected fragments with '.', so the SMILES is '*C(*)=O.*N*'.

planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question instruction that asks for the SMILES expression of the transition-state structure and specifically says to ignore the arrows, so do not encode electron-pushing arrows or a forming N-C bond.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use SMILES rules: unspecified R groups in a generic reaction drawing can be encoded as wildcard atoms '*'; single bonds to wildcards may be implicit; a carbonyl is written as C=O; disconnected fragments are separated by a dot; the N-H hydrogen can be implicit for neutral amine nitrogen in SMILES.
